status of photonics regardless of interconnects or computing or sensing: we do not have a common standard for how to make wires to cross each other. The year is 2026, and people are still simulating MMI waveguide crossing by hand.
Why are the foundries not publishing PDKs with a full suite of simulations for the corresponding components together with the configs and materials properties instead of a few mere scalar spec numbers? Does the simulation layer need to be fully democratized for something similar to this to happen? The form of info exchange is too primitive, and the rate of the exchange is too low.

2 will hopefully change over time. Design alone is also getting so much easier, bottleneck is foundry willingness to test it out and speed of real world iteration.
3 echos 1, incompetence across the stack. Design should be abundant, and scarcity is real world testing and iteration, and bittlenecked by form and rate of info exchange. e.g. if the packaging house is not within the foundry, both the communication and the full process iteration could be even more than 2x slower.
4: COUPE still sucks, tsmc is late to the party, they need to get kicked, but they are also the privileged and not as motivated. At least they've decided photonics is important and real enough.
At the end of the day volume and demand motivates better workflow, and many workflow and language things are described and exchanged in current state of the photonics industry need to change. Interconnect needs could do a lot to the industry, and we might see actual proliferation of a lot of other photonics applications the academics have been dreaming abt on paper.
